messages.subject: vector memory issues with gl.genleastcost
parts:
Hey All,

I'm trying to run the gl.genleastcost for a species with a "C" distribuiton, so euclidean distance is not useful. I keep getting a "Error: vector memory exhausted (limit reached?)" situation.

I'm wondering what is the most likely cause here (I'm running it on a very big and powerful computer.
  • Is it that my raster layer has too fine a scale and too big (it's from a DEM and I could aggregate to larger grid squares, it's a bit part of Australia)
  • Is it that my raster layer has a bit set of NA in the middle (the Eyre basin)?
  • Is it that I have too many individuals (116)?
  • Is it that I have too many SNPs (707)?
Thanks!

Renee

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: Re: vector memory issues with gl.genleastcost
parts:
Hi Renee,

there are some problems with memory with the cost distance function. My experience is that it works okay if your raster is not larger than 1000 x 1000 cells. If larger you may run into trouble. So definitely for a first run try to reduce the raster dimensions if they are much higher than 1000 x 1000.

Missing values (NA) should be fine, but you need to make sure you are not "starting" in a missing value square, this breaks the function. My trick here is to set the resistance on missing values (e.g. lakes) to ridiculously high values (e.g. 10000) (which makes sure it is avoided). Nevertheless if you start in high resistance areas the resistance values are off.

SNPs are fine (independent of cost matrix distance calculation). Individuals 116 is definitely on the high side and hence calculation of distances will take a while (116*115/2 = 6670 distances). I would simply try to run it with a subset of individuals and check if they work (where you are sure they are not in a missing value area). Finally if all fails you can try to use circuitscape for distance calculations. I have some code somewhere how to run circuitscape from R, but need to dig for it. So let me know if that is interesting for you.

All the best and cheers, Bernd
